structure:
repos/trade-imports-stub is a Java / Spring Boot stub service (port 8087) standing in for third-party integrations: the Trade Platform OAuth token endpoint and MDM reference data through APIM (both called by trade-imports-reference-data), and AWS STS, Entra and the address lookup gateway (called by trade-imports-ins-backend). Code is in src/main/java/uk/gov/defra/trade/imports/: stubs/federated (AddressLookupSimulatorController 163 lines, plus the STS and Entra simulators), stubs/mdm (MdmStubResponses 14 lines; countries/CountriesController 52 lines; poe/PortsOfEntryController 34 lines; product/ProductController 128 lines), utils/FileUtils (30 lines), and the latency, faults, configuration, filter and exception plumbing. Saved MDM responses are in src/main/resources/responses/: countriesResponse.json (10,530 lines, a JSON array of 250 country records ordered by MDM id, not by name; each carries id, countryUUID, ISONumeric, alpha2, alpha3, independent, system, systemAlias, systemAlpha2, systemAlpha3, effectiveAlias, effectiveAlpha2, effectiveAlpha3, subDivisions and blocks; 32 records carry the GBNAG_SPS_EX block, and 4 carry a subdivision or a system alias), portsOfEntryResponse.json (1,252 lines, {result: [...]} holding 78 port records with id, activeFrom, activeTo, code, name, townCity, county, postCode, countryCode, traffic and status), and three product files (mdmProductSearchResponses 11,215 lines, mdmProductCommoditiesResponses 7,542, mdmProductSpeciesResponses 3,153). Tests in src/test/java mirror each controller, with FileUtilsTest and the MdmStub* test helpers. The scope takes in only the address lookup simulator (its searches, addresses and postcodes) and the MDM countries and ports endpoints with their saved records, the blocks parameter and the shared MDM response plumbing. It is cut into 6 parts: the address lookup simulator; the countries endpoint with the shared MDM code and tests; the 250 country records in three consecutive runs of the JSON file cut on record boundaries; and the ports endpoint with its 78 records. Left out by the scope: the MDM product endpoints and their three saved files (the commodity catalogue waits on MDM), the STS and Entra simulators, the trade token stub, latency profiles, fault injection, metrics, proxy, TLS, Mongo, logging and CI config.

Extracted in 6 parts:
Part 1, Address lookup simulator: Part 1, the address lookup simulator. Read in full: src/main/java/uk/gov/defra/trade/imports/stubs/federated/AddressLookupSimulatorController.java (163 lines: one GET route, a bearer check, a switch over reserved search terms, a three-addresses fixture and a no-results fixture), its test AddressLookupSimulatorControllerTest.java (194 lines, 14 tests), application.yml (the address-lookup-simulator block, lines 103 to 104, read with the whole file), application-local.yml (30 lines, no address-lookup override) and README.md's Federated-credential simulators section (lines 67 to 74). Covered: the route, the postcode and find parameters and their 400, the eight reserved terms (SW1A 1AA, ZZ1 1ZZ, QQ1 1QQ, XX1 1XX, YY1 1YY, TT1 1TT, Buckingham Palace, Downing Street) and what each answers, every field of the 3 fixture addresses, the default no-results answer, the bearer signature, audience and expiry check with its 401 body, the expected-audience default, and every test. Left to other parts: the STS and Entra simulators that issue the tokens.
Part 2, MDM countries endpoint and shared MDM plumbing: Part 2, the MDM countries endpoint and shared MDM plumbing. Read in full: stubs/mdm/countries/CountriesController.java (52 lines: one GET /mdm/geo/countries handler, the subscription-key header, the system and blocks parameters, the block filter), stubs/mdm/MdmStubResponses.java (14 lines: the header name and the trace header every MDM answer carries), utils/FileUtils.java (30 lines: loads a saved JSON response from the classpath), the tests CountriesControllerTest (7 tests, one parameterised over two blank values), FileUtilsTest (5 tests, two of them about the ports file, claimed here only as what this test class proves), and the helpers MdmStubWebMvcTest, MdmStubRequests and MdmStubResponseMatchers; application.yml's stub-latency block (the mdm and trade-token integrations); README.md's latency-profiles integrations table and its MDM countries and border control posts section. Covered: the countries route and its inputs, the blocks filter rules, the trace header, file loading and its failure, every test as what it proves, and the MDM integration's paths, interface name, owner and latency defaults. Not covered here: the country records' content beyond what the tests assert (parts 3 to 5) and the ports endpoint (part 6).
Part 3, Country records 1 to 83: Part 3 read lines 1 to 3418 of src/main/resources/responses/countriesResponse.json in full: the opening of the JSON array and its first 83 country records, from Aruba (record 1, line 2) to Martinique (record 83, ending at line 3418). Each record is one object with id and countryUUID (content, schemeId, schemeAgencyId), ISONumeric, alpha2 and alpha3 (value, listId, listAgencyId, listVersionId), independent, system, systemAlias, systemAlpha2, systemAlpha3, effectiveAlias, effectiveAlpha2, effectiveAlpha3, subDivisions and blocks. Records run in ascending order of their MDM id, so the names are in no alphabetical order. In this slice no record has a subdivision or a system alias, three records (Chad, Oman, Cuba) have no independent key, and 10 records carry two block entries each: an unnamed entry and GBNAG_SPS_EX (Hungary, Latvia, Cyprus, Greece, Czechia, Denmark, Malta, Switzerland, Slovakia, Poland). Claims 001 to 018 are the shapes and rules every record in the slice shares; 019 to 101 are one claim per record, in file order; 102 to 121 are the block memberships, two per blocked record.
Part 4, Country records 84 to 166: Part 4 read lines 3419 to 7053 of src/main/resources/responses/countriesResponse.json in full: 83 consecutive country records (records 84 to 166 of the 250, in MDM id order), from Philippines (the) to Saint Martin (French part). Each record has the same shape: id and countryUUID (MDM-COUNTRY, DEFRA), ISONumeric, alpha2 and alpha3 (ISO-3166-3, 2024-06), independent, system, systemAlias, systemAlpha2, systemAlpha3, effectiveAlias, effectiveAlpha2, effectiveAlpha3, subDivisions and blocks. Covered: one claim per record with its effective and ISO codes, ISONumeric, independent and system; one claim per GBNAG_SPS_EX membership (14 countries) and one per country for its nameless block entries; one claim per subdivision (6 for France, 2 for Portugal); and slice-wide claims on the shared list metadata, id shape, null system aliases, unpadded ISO numerics, MDM id ordering, Togo's missing independent key and the French territories that appear both as subdivisions and as countries. No record in the slice has a non-null systemAlias, systemAlpha2 or systemAlpha3.
Part 5, Country records 167 to 250: Part 5 read lines 7054 to 10530 of repos/trade-imports-stub/src/main/resources/responses/countriesResponse.json in full: country records 167 to 250 of the 250-record JSON array, in file order (ascending MDM id, not by name), from Timor-Leste (line 7054) to Austria (line 10480), and the array's closing bracket at line 10530. Each record is about 40 lines (50 with blocks, more with a subdivision): id and countryUUID objects, ISONumeric, alpha2 and alpha3 objects each with value and ISO list metadata, independent, system, systemAlias, systemAlpha2, systemAlpha3, effectiveAlias, effectiveAlpha2, effectiveAlpha3, subDivisions and blocks. It covered all 84 records, one claim each with every field the scope names (claims 001 to 084, numbered record minus 166); the two subdivisions (GB-NIR on the GB record and ES-CN Canary Islands on Spain) with their ids, codes, names, categories and blocs; and every block membership country by country (GBNAG_SPS_EX on Lithuania, Bulgaria, Liechtenstein, the United Kingdom, Spain, Sweden, Slovenia and Austria, plus the unnamed block entries they carry). It also records what the slice shows across records: no system aliases, no independent true and four records without the key, the GB record with no effectiveAlias, the Canary Islands both as a country and as Spain's subdivision with a null ISONumeric, the ISO list metadata, the unpadded numeric codes, the ISO-style display names, and the id ordering.
Part 6, MDM ports of entry: Part 6, MDM ports of entry. Read in full: PortsOfEntryController.java (one GET handler at /mdm/trade/bcp/poes taking the Ocp-Apim-Subscription-Key header and an optional system parameter, answering the fixture loaded at start-up with the shared trace header), PortsOfEntryControllerTest.java (three tests: whole list in MDM order, traffic types, missing key refused), MdmStubResponses.java (the header name and trace-header helper, used here; the shared plumbing itself is part 2's), MdmStubRequests.java (the test helper that adds the key), and portsOfEntryResponse.json (a result array of 78 port records, 16 lines each, with id, activeFrom, activeTo, code, name, townCity, county, postCode, countryCode, traffic and status). Claims 001-036 cover the endpoint, its header and parameter, the response shape, counts of traffic types (Airport 18, Port 59, Rail 1) and statuses (all active, Approved-Live), the empty-field, duplicate-name and odd-copy records, each test, and three gaps. Claims 037-114 are one per port record, in saved order.

claims.statement: The stub simulates the DEFRA address lookup gateway's address search at GET /simulator/address-lookup/v2.1/addresses.
The stub simulates AWS STS, Entra and the address lookup gateway for the address lookup in trade-imports-ins-backend.
claims.quote: The stub simulates AWS STS, Entra and the address lookup gateway for the address lookup in `trade-imports-ins-backend`.

claims.statement: The address search takes two optional query parameters, postcode and find.
claims.quote:
@RequestParam(required = false) String postcode,
        @RequestParam(required = false) String find)

claims.statement: The simulator treats postcode and find identically: the same reserved terms give the same answers whichever parameter carries them.
claims.note: The comment says what find really matches (a postcode, a building name or number, a street, a town) is a question only the real gateway can answer, and dev settles the behaviour.

claims.statement: When both postcode and find are given, the simulator searches on postcode and ignores find, because the term is postcode whenever postcode is present.
claims.quote: String term = postcode != null ? postcode : find;

claims.statement: A search with neither postcode nor find answers 400 with a JSON body whose message is "Either postcode or find is required".
The bearer token is checked before the search parameters, so a request with a bad token and no search term answers 401, not 400.
The search term SW1A 1AA answers 200 with JSON holding three addresses.
The three-addresses answer has a header whose totalResults is the string "3", and a results array.

claims.statement: The fixture is shaped like the real dev gateway response of 2026-09-17, not the published v2.1 specification: everything upper case, country free text rather than an ISO code, no county field, match a string and counts as strings.
claims.quote: Shaped like the real dev response of 2026-09-17, not like the published v2.1 specification: everything upper case, {@code country} free text rather than an ISO code, no county field, {@code match} a string, and counts as strings.

claims.statement: The search term ZZ1 1ZZ answers 204 No Content with no body.
The search term QQ1 1QQ answers 400 with a JSON body whose message is "Requested postcode is not valid".
Only the reserved term QQ1 1QQ triggers the invalid-postcode 400: the simulator does not check postcode format, so any other malformed postcode answers the no-results fixture.
claims.note: The switch has no format check; every term not listed falls to the default branch.

claims.statement: The search term XX1 1XX answers 503 with a JSON body whose message is "Service Unavailable".
claims.note: The test calls it the reserved throttled postcode.

claims.statement: The search term YY1 1YY answers 200 with an HTML body, not JSON: "<html><body>Bad Gateway</body></html>".
claims.note: The test calls it the reserved proxy-error postcode.

claims.statement: The search term TT1 1TT waits 15 seconds and then answers 200 with the three-addresses fixture.
claims.note: delayedOk calls Thread.sleep(15_000) then jsonOk(THREE_ADDRESSES_FIXTURE). No test covers this term.

claims.statement: The free-text search terms "Buckingham Palace" and "Downing Street" answer 200 with the three-addresses fixture.
The reserved free-text terms are fixtures for demonstrating find, not a model of what find matches: a result from the simulator says nothing about whether the same search returns results in dev.
claims.quote: These are reserved terms like the postcodes above, NOT a model of what find matches — that is the question the spike exists to answer, and only the real gateway can. A search here returning results says nothing about whether the same search would return results in dev.

claims.statement: Any search term that is not reserved answers 200 with a no-results JSON body: totalResults the string "0" and an empty results array.
Reserved terms match exactly and case-sensitively, so a partial term such as "Buckingham", a lower-case "sw1a 1aa" or a postcode without its space answers no results.
claims.note: A Java string switch is exact and case-sensitive, and the term is not trimmed or normalised. The "Buckingham" case is proven by addresses_shouldReturnNoResults_forFreeTextThatIsNotReserved.

claims.statement: Every answer the simulator gives that is not 204 or the HTML proxy error is JSON.
The simulator checks the bearer token the way a real resource server would: signature, audience and expiry, before serving any fixture.
claims.quote: Checks the bearer token the way a real resource server would — signature, audience, expiry — before serving the reserved-postcode fixtures

claims.statement: A request with no Authorization header, or one that does not start with "Bearer " (case-insensitive), answers 401.
A bearer that is not a parseable signed JWT answers 401.
A bearer whose RSA signature does not verify against the simulator's Entra signing key answers 401.
claims.note: So only a token issued by the stub's own Entra simulator is accepted.

claims.statement: A bearer whose audience is missing or does not contain the expected audience answers 401, and the simulator logs a warning naming the audience it rejected.
claims.quote: log.warn("Address lookup simulator rejected a bearer with audience {}", claims.getAudience());

claims.statement: A bearer with no expiry time, or one whose expiry has passed, answers 401.
claims.quote:
if (claims.getExpirationTime() == null || claims.getExpirationTime().before(new Date())) {
            return unauthorized();

claims.statement: Every 401 answers the JSON body { "statusCode": 401, "message": "Unauthorized. Access token is missing or invalid." }, word for word what the real gateway's validate-jwt policy returned in dev on 2026-09-17.
claims.quote: { \"statusCode\": 401, \"message\": \"Unauthorized. Access token is missing or invalid.\" }

claims.statement: A 401 carries no WWW-Authenticate header, matching the real gateway.
claims.quote: The gateway sends no {@code WWW-Authenticate} header with it, and neither does this.

claims.statement: The expected audience is set by address-lookup-simulator.expected-audience, from ADDRESS_LOOKUP_SIMULATOR_EXPECTED_AUDIENCE, defaulting to api://33333333-3333-3333-3333-333333333333.
The expected audience must match the Scope that ins-backend requests once /.default is stripped, api:// prefix included; the dev gateway rejects the bare GUID, so the simulator does too.
claims.quote: `address-lookup-simulator.expected-audience` must match the `Scope` that ins-backend requests once `/.default` is stripped, `api://` prefix included. The gateway in dev rejects the bare GUID, so the simulator does too.

claims.statement: The local profile does not change the address lookup simulator's settings, so a locally run stub expects the same default audience.
claims.note: The local profile overrides only the STS issuer among the simulators; it has no address-lookup-simulator block.

claims.statement: The class Javadoc says find and the truncation and find fixtures are a later iteration, though the controller now handles find and two free-text fixtures; no truncation fixture exists.
claims.quote: Only the fixtures iteration 1 needs are wired here; {@code find} and the truncation/find fixtures are iteration 2.
claims.note: The Javadoc is stale against the code below it on find. A truncation fixture (more results than a page holds) is named but not built.

claims.statement: The simulator has no fixture that returns more than three addresses, an address outside England, a Welsh-language address or a paged result; it takes no parameter other than postcode and find.
claims.note: Looked at every case of the switch and both fixtures. The Javadoc names truncation fixtures as not built.

claims.statement: Test addresses_shouldReturnThreeFixtureAddresses_forTheDefaultPostcode proves postcode SW1A 1AA with a valid bearer answers 200 JSON with totalResults "3" and contains DOWNING STREET.
Test addresses_shouldReturnAddressesShapedLikeTheRealApi proves the SW1A 1AA answer has subBuildingName BUCKINGHAM PALACE, country ENGLAND, match "1" as a string, and no county anywhere.

Test addresses_shouldReject_whenTheBearerAudienceIsTheBareGuidRatherThanTheApiUri proves a bearer whose audience is the bare GUID answers 401 with the gateway's exact body and no WWW-Authenticate header.
claims.note: The test comment says this is the exact mismatch the spike hit in dev, and that the missing header is why Spring's authorization failure handler cannot evict a stale token.

claims.statement: Test addresses_shouldServeTheReservedFreeTextTerms_soFindCanBeDemonstrated proves find=Buckingham Palace answers 200 containing BUCKINGHAM PALACE.
Test addresses_shouldReturnNoResults_forFreeTextThatIsNotReserved proves find=Buckingham answers 200 with totalResults "0".
Test addresses_shouldReturn400_whenNeitherPostcodeNorFindIsGiven proves a request with a valid bearer and no search term answers 400 containing "Either postcode or find is required".
Test addresses_shouldReturn204_forTheReservedNoResultsPostcode proves postcode ZZ1 1ZZ answers 204.
Test addresses_shouldReturnARejectedPostcode400_forTheReservedInvalidPostcode proves postcode QQ1 1QQ answers 400 containing "Requested postcode".
Test addresses_shouldReturn503_forTheReservedThrottledPostcode proves postcode XX1 1XX answers 503.
Test addresses_shouldReturnNonJsonHtml_forTheReservedProxyErrorPostcode proves postcode YY1 1YY answers 200 with an HTML content type.
Test addresses_shouldReject_whenNoBearerPresent proves a search with no Authorization header answers 401.
Test addresses_shouldReject_whenTheBearerAudienceIsWrong proves a bearer with audience api://SomethingElse answers 401.
Test addresses_shouldReject_whenTheBearerHasExpired proves a bearer that expired 60 seconds ago answers 401.
Test addresses_shouldReject_whenTheBearerSignatureIsWrong proves a bearer signed by a different key, with the right audience and a future expiry, answers 401.
No test covers the 15-second delayed search term TT1 1TT, the free-text term Downing Street, or a request that gives both postcode and find.
claims.note: Walked all 14 tests; none uses TT1 1TT, Downing Street as a term, or both parameters.

claims.statement: The stub answers GET /mdm/geo/countries, standing in for MDM's countries endpoint through APIM.
The countries endpoint requires an Ocp-Apim-Subscription-Key request header.
Any value of the subscription-key header is accepted: the stub never checks it.
claims.note: The handler never reads ocpApimSubscriptionKey, and the tests send an arbitrary value and get 200.

claims.statement: A call to the countries endpoint without the subscription-key header is refused with 400 Bad Request.
claims.note: The 400 is Spring's own answer for a missing required header; the README says GlobalExceptionHandler answers only application exceptions.

claims.statement: The countries endpoint accepts an optional system query parameter and ignores it: the answer is the same whatever system is given.
claims.note: system is bound but never used in the handler body.

claims.statement: The countries endpoint accepts an optional blocks query parameter.
When blocks is absent or blank, the countries endpoint answers the whole saved country list.
claims.quote: JsonNode body = blocks == null || blocks.isBlank() ? countries : inBlock(countries, blocks);

claims.statement: When blocks names a block, the countries endpoint answers only the country records that carry a block entry whose name equals it exactly.
claims.note: Only the record's top-level blocks array is read; a subdivision's blocs are not consulted. The match is case-sensitive and blocks is a single name, not a list.

claims.statement: A filtered countries answer keeps the saved file's order.
The blocks filter keeps a record carrying the block whatever that block entry's includeCountry says, as MDM does.
claims.quote: `blocks` keeps the records that carry that block whatever `includeCountry` says, as MDM does.

claims.statement: The saved country records hold membership of the GBNAG_SPS_EX block only, so any other block answers an empty list.
claims.quote: The saved records hold the membership of `GBNAG_SPS_EX` only, so any other block answers an empty list.

claims.statement: The countries endpoint answers 200 with a JSON array as its body, both whole and filtered.
The countries endpoint serves the country records saved from MDM in responses/countriesResponse.json.

claims.statement: independent does not say whether a country is sovereign: it is false for sovereign states such as Japan, Canada and the United States as well as for territories such as Aruba and Greenland.
claims.note: Inferred because the same false value sits on every record that has the key, whatever its status, so nothing in the slice can tell a country from a territory.

claims.statement: The list served as countries includes territories, dependencies and Crown Dependencies alongside states, among them Aruba, Reunion, American Samoa, Greenland, Jersey, the Isle of Man, the British Indian Ocean Territory, the Cocos (Keeling) Islands, Bonaire, Sint Eustatius and Saba, Sint Maarten, the Aland Islands, Guadeloupe, Martinique and the United States Minor Outlying Islands.

claims.statement: effectiveAlias names follow the ISO 3166 short-name style, with the definite article in brackets after the name: "Niger (the)", "Cook Islands (the)", "Turks and Caicos Islands (the)", "United States of America (the)", "Marshall Islands (the)" and "Syrian Arab Republic (the)".

Other effectiveAlias names use the ISO long-form qualifiers in brackets or after a comma: "Moldova (the Republic of)", "Bolivia (Plurinational State of)", "Korea (the Democratic People's Republic of)", "Palestine, State of", "Saint Helena, Ascension and Tristan da Cunha", "Virgin Islands (British)" and "Sint Maarten (Dutch part)".
effectiveAlias names are written without diacritics: "Reunion", "Saint Barthelemy" and "Aland Islands".

10 of the 83 records carry block entries, two each: Hungary, Latvia, Cyprus, Greece, Czechia, Denmark, Malta, Switzerland, Slovakia and Poland. The other 73 have an empty blocks list. No block entry in the slice has a tag, and every entry has includeCountry true.
claims.note: Switzerland is in the GBNAG_SPS_EX block with the nine EU members of the slice. What the block means is not stated in this file.

claims.statement: The slice does not say what the GBNAG_SPS_EX block stands for or which block the unnamed first entry of each blocked record belongs to.
claims.ref: src/main/resources/responses/countriesResponse.json:440-450 (Hungary's blocks, the first in the slice); looked through every block entry in lines 1 to 3418
claims.note: The block name is a code only, and the unnamed entry has no name key. How the stub filters on the blocks parameter belongs to the countries endpoint part.

claims.statement: The stub answers GET /mdm/trade/bcp/poes with the list of ports of entry.
The ports of entry call must carry an Ocp-Apim-Subscription-Key header.
The stub accepts any value in the subscription key header: the handler never reads the value, and the tests send "any-value-at-all".
claims.note: The value is bound to a parameter the method body does not use.

claims.statement: A ports of entry call with no subscription key header is refused with 400 Bad Request.
The ports of entry call takes an optional system query parameter.
The system parameter changes nothing: the stub answers the same records whatever system is named, or none.
claims.note: The system parameter is bound but never used in the body.

claims.statement: The ports of entry call answers 200 OK.
The ports of entry response carries the header x-ms-middleware-request-id with the value stub-trace-id.
claims.note: The shared trace-header helper is part 2's to claim; this claim records only that this endpoint uses it.

claims.statement: The stub answers the saved port records whole: every record, unfiltered and unchanged, in the order they are saved.
The stub reads the saved port records once, when it starts, and answers every call from that copy.
claims.note: mechanism: loads the ports fixture into memory at start-up; a change to the file needs a restart.

claims.statement: The ports of entry response body is an object whose result field holds the array of port records.
The stub returns 78 port records.
Each port record has the fields id, activeFrom, activeTo, code, name, townCity, county, postCode, countryCode, traffic and status, and status has a code and a description.
claims.note: Every one of the 78 records has exactly this set of keys.

claims.statement: Each port record carries a UUID as its id.
